MFL – French
At Chalfont Valley, we teach French in Key Stage 2. Our French curriculum aims to instil a love of language learning and an awareness of other cultures. We want pupils to develop the confidence to communicate in French for practical purposes, using both written and spoken French.
Through our curriculum, we aim to give pupils a foundation for language learning that encourages and enables them to apply their skills to learning further languages, develop a strong understanding of the English language, facilitate future study, and open opportunities to study and work in other countries.

Academy Day
THE SCHOOL DAY
The children are asked to be accompanied by an adult at all times whilst waiting to go into school.
At the start of the day:
8.30am The main gates open.
At the start of the school day, we ask parents to walk their children onto the playground and drop them at their collection point. Children will be asked to line up behind their cone while we ask parents to remain on the playground and stand back from the class collection points, behind the yellow line that marks the edge of the netball court. This will prevent overcrowding and ensure all children can be seen clearly by their teachers and parents/carers. Parents should remain on the playground to supervise their children until their class teacher is with their class. Year 6 children may walk to school and line up on their own.
8.40am Class teacher will be out on the palyground to greet the children.
EYFS children should be dropped off directly at the EYFS gate. We ask that EYFS parents use the path, rather than the playground. We respectfully ask EYFS parents to be mindful of other year groups coming into school as you drop off your child. Please wait for any moving classes to pass before moving to/ from the EYFS gate to ensure the classes remains together.
8.45am Children go into school to be registered.
At the end of the day:
3.15pm Class teacher will bring children out to the playground.
At the end of the school day, class teachers will walk their classes to their designated class collection point where they will be lined up. Class teachers will then release children to their adults from their line.
When you arrive at Chalfont Valley to collect your children, we kindly ask all parents to stand back from the class collection points, behind the yellow line that marks the edge of the netball court. This will prevent overcrowding and ensure all children and teachers can see parents/carers clearly.
Children to be released from the EYFS gate. EYFS parents to use the entrance path, rather than the playground. We respectfully ask EYFS parents to be mindful of other year groups coming out of school as you collect your child. Please wait for any passing classes to pass before moving to/ from the EYFS gate to ensure the class remains together.
The total hours the pupils are at school amounts to 32.5 hours.

Maths
Mathematics is a powerful creative discipline that helps us understand and shape the world. We want all pupils at Chalfont Valley to experience the beauty, power, and enjoyment of mathematics and develop a sense of curiosity about the subject.
We believe that all children can achieve in mathematics and strive to foster secure and deep understanding of mathematical concepts. We embrace mistakes and misconceptions as valuable learning opportunities and provide challenges through rich and sophisticated problems. At Chalfont Valley, we cultivate an appreciation for numbers and number operations, enabling efficient, fluent, and accurate mental calculations and written procedures. This is fundamental to children’s mathematical success. We aim for all children to recall basic number facts (e.g., number bonds, multiplication, and division facts) quickly and accurately.
We follow the Can Do Maths program, which employs a cyclical unit structure to allow children to revisit themes, make connections, and deepen their understanding. Our teaching focuses on developing secure and deep understanding, utilizing practical resources and iconic representations to support learning and memorization. We avoid teaching “rules” and “tricks” without understanding and limit the use of only “standard” examples, as these can contribute to learners feeling they “can’t do” math.
All learners need to believe they can succeed, and they need to feel supported by their teacher and parents. Adopting a growth mindset is central to the “Can Do Maths” approach, including the use of “yet” and recognizing that making mistakes is a natural part of learning. Negative phrases like “Don’t worry, I can’t do math” or “Math is too hard” can hinder learners’ belief in their abilities.
Success in mathematics comes from hard work. While the subject can be challenging at times, perseverance and effort are key to achieving success.
